White’s 1.c4 controls d5 and prepares quick development, but it creates no immediate tactical threat. Black should claim central space and plan harmonious development. Playing 1...e5 controls d4, opens lines for the f8 bishop and queen, and is tactically safe since the c4-pawn does not attack e5. Black can follow with ...Nc6, ...d6, and kingside castling.

Move: e5

Black’s e5-pawn controls d4 and f4, so White should develop while avoiding a quick pawn kick. Moves like 2.Nf3 allow ...e4, forcing the knight to move again. 2.Nc3 is more solid: it develops a piece, controls d5, and keeps flexible plans with g3/Bg2 or d3/e3.

Move: Nc3

Black should develop and fight for the center. White’s Nc3 eyes d5 and e4, so Black’s most natural reply is to develop the kingside knight to f6, attacking e4/d5 and preparing quick castling. It also keeps flexible options like ...Nc6 and ...d5, while avoiding any immediate tactics.

Move: Nf6
